facts.value: Christianity is based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth as presented in the New Testament.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: The Christian faith is essentially faith in Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God, and as Savior and Lord.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Almost all Christians believe in the Trinity, which teaches the unity of Father, Son (Jesus Christ), and Holy Spirit as three persons in one Godhead.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Most Christians can describe their faith with the Nicene Creed.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Christianity has been propagated throughout the world via missionary work and was the religion of the Byzantine Empire in the first millennium and of Western Europe during the time of colonization.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Christianity is the world's largest religion, with about 2.3 billion followers as of 2015.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: The main divisions of Christianity include the Catholic Church, Eastern Christianity, and Protestantism.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: The Catholic Church is led by the Bishop of Rome and is a communion of 24 Churches, including the Latin Church and 23 Eastern Catholic churches.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Eastern Christianity includes Eastern Orthodoxy, Oriental Orthodoxy, and the Church of the East.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Protestantism separated from the Catholic Church in the 16th-century Protestant Reformation and is split into thousands of denominations.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Major branches of Protestantism include Anglicanism, Baptists, Calvinism, Lutheranism, and Methodism.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Smaller groups include Restorationism, the Latter-day Saint movement, and Jehovah's Witnesses.
